official.deadline_note: No single ADB-published deadline: ADB instructs applicants to send the completed application to the designated institution at least six (6) months before the intended intake; each institution publishes its own intake month and application deadline.
official.application_cycle: No central cycle - institution-led intake; send the application at least six months prior to the planned commencement of studies.
official.status_note: Program is ongoing and active: ADB's 2025 Annual Report records 131 scholarships awarded in 2025, and ADB continues to direct applicants to request information and application forms from the 27 designated institutions with no closing date advertised.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "Full tuition fees" (ADB-Japan Scholarship Program, 'What We Offer'); confirmed in the FAQ as "full tuition fees".
benefits: For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for thesis preparation; computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered in special circumstances
eligibility: Be a national of an ADB borrowing member country and Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible country (41 countries/areas listed by ADB)
Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country
Have gained admission to an approved master's course at a Designated Institution
Hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent with superior academic record
Have at least two (2) years of full-time professional working experience acquired after a university degree at the time of application
Not be more than 35 years old at the time of application, unless waived in exceptional cases with the expressed endorsement of the Government of Japan
Be in good health; agree to return and work in your home country for at least two (2) years after completion of studies

Not be an ADB Executive Director, Alternate Director, management, staff or consultant (or their close relatives), not staff of a Designated Institution, not living or working outside your home country, and not already enrolled in a graduate degree program
requirements: Proficiency in oral and written English communication skills to be able to pursue studies
At least two (2) years of full-time professional working experience acquired after a university degree at the time of application
A bachelor's degree or its equivalent with a superior academic record
Admission to an approved master's course at one of the 27 Designated Institutions
Good health at the time of application
Age not more than 35 years at the time of application (waiver only in exceptional cases endorsed by the Government of Japan)
documents: Completed institution application form for admission to the Designated Institution
ADB-Japan Scholarship Program Information Sheet (application form)
Latest Income Tax Return or Certification of Annual/Monthly Salary, whichever is available
selection_criteria: Qualifications of the candidate, with priority to the ranking or order of merit proposed by the Designated Institutions
Preference to women candidates and to applicants with lesser financial capacity
In principle, no support to applicants who have previously studied abroad or who are pursuing a second master's degree
Candidates applying at a Designated Institution in their own country may not be selected
Diversity of nationalities in the overall program and at each Designated Institution

Preference to candidates with higher potential to occupy senior positions in development-related work; proposed fields of study must be closely linked to the candidate's academic background and professional experience and align with ADB's Strategy 2030 priority areas and/or Japan's ODA priority issues
coverage: Not covered: the scholar's family expenses; extra-curricular courses or training; additional travel during the study program; supplementary educational materials, field trips, or participation in workshops, seminars or internships; purchase of educational equipment such as computers
application_method: Request information and application forms from the chosen academic institution(s), using institution websites, handbooks and in-country information sessions
Indicate to the academic institution that you are applying for admission and wish to be considered for the ADB-JSP Scholarship
Submit the completed institution application form and required documentation, including the ADB-JSP application sheet, to the academic institution at least six (6) months before the intended intake
The institution screens and ranks applicants under its own selection criteria against ADB's eligibility and selection criteria, then sends its ranked list (with its score/grading system) to ADB
ADB reviews the submissions and recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval
The institution informs all applicants of the outcome and arranges the signing of the Acceptance of Scholarship Award, in which scholars agree to return to their home country after studies
official.application_route: Apply directly to your chosen Designated Institution(s) for admission and ADB-JSP consideration - there is no separate application to ADB; the institution ranks and nominates candidates for ADB and Japan's Executive Director to approve.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a national of an ADB borrowing member country and Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible country (ADB's published list of 41 countries/areas), must not hold dual citizenship of any developed country, and must not be living or working in a country other than your home country.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the program is built for citizens of ADB's developing member economies studying across the region; study may be at any of the 27 Designated Institutions in Asia and the Pacific (17 in Japan), though ADB warns that candidates applying at an institution in their own country may not be selected.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only courses listed as approved fields of study at the participating institutions qualify: postgraduate studies in economics, management, health, education, agriculture, environment, natural resource management, science and technology, and other development-related fields.
official.duration: One (1) year, with extension to the second year of study as appropriate conditional on satisfactory performance; the maximum duration of the scholarship award is two (2) years for the master's program.
official.description: Established in April 1988 with financing from the Government of Japan, the ADB-Japan Scholarship Program offers citizens of ADB's developing member countries the opportunity to pursue graduate studies in economics, business and management, science and technology, and other development-related fields at 27 selected educational institutions across Asia and the Pacific, 17 of them in Japan. Scholars are expected to return to their home countries after their studies to apply and share their new knowledge and skills to promote socioeconomic development.
official.program_type: Graduate (master's) scholarship program financed by the Government of Japan and administered by the Asian Development Bank
official.english_requirement: Applicants must have proficiency in oral and written English communication skills to be able to pursue studies; ADB publishes no specific IELTS/TOEFL score (each Designated Institution sets its own admission language requirements).

verification.notes: Verified against ADB's own pages on adb.org (programme, FAQ, procedures, August 2026 brochure PDF and 2025 Annual Report PDF): benefits package, eligibility rules, selection criteria, required documents, duration and the six-month submission rule are all published verbatim; ADB publishes no per-scholar monetary amount and no central deadline, so the funding and deadline fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a genuinely full master's package - full tuition, a monthly subsistence and housing allowance, books, medical insurance and travel - but there is no application to ADB itself: you apply for admission to one of the 27 designated institutions and flag that you want ADB-JSP consideration, and the institution ranks and nominates you up the chain. There is no central deadline; ADB's rule is that complete applications reach the institution at least six months before your intended intake, so the deadline that actually binds you is the one at the institution you target. Your odds rest less on any single test score and more on your two-plus years of post-degree work experience, a field of study that lines up with ADB Strategy 2030 or Japan's ODA priorities, and how strongly your institution nominates you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career professionals from ADB developing member countries with 2+ years of post-degree work experience and a development-focused master's plan at a designated institution, who intend to return home afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on ADB's published 41-country eligibility list and that you hold no dual citizenship of any developed country
Pick a course from the approved fields of study at one of the 27 designated institutions - courses outside the list cannot be funded
Download both the institution's own application form and ADB's JSP Information Sheet; they travel together in one package
Obtain your latest income tax return or annual/monthly salary certification, plus a separate certification of family (parents') income - these ADB-specific documents are easy to miss
Work backwards from your target intake: submit at least six months ahead and confirm the institution's actual deadline
Do not resign your job or make irreversible plans until the institution confirms an award - admission alone is not selection
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a designated institution in your own country - ADB warns such candidates may not be selected
Having previously studied abroad, or holding/pursuing a second master's degree - both are principle-level exclusions
A proposed field of study not closely linked to your academic background and professional experience
Failing to secure the institution's nomination: only admitted, institution-endorsed candidates are considered by ADB, so a weak institutional ranking is decisive
Incomplete or inaccurate documentation, which ADB says may mean the application is not processed, or an award terminated if falsity is later found
Being over 35 without Japan's exceptional endorsement, or lacking the required two years of full-time post-degree experience
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: ADB does not cover the scholar's family expenses, extra-curricular courses or training, additional travel during the study program, supplementary educational materials, field trips, or participation in workshops, seminars or internships, or purchase of educational equipment such as computers - applicants fund these themselves.
document_audit: The ADB-JSP Information Sheet is separate from the university's admission form - both must be submitted to the institution
Income proof means the latest income tax return OR certification of annual/monthly salary, plus a separate certification of family (parents') income
All copies of academic records must accompany the package, sent to the institution at least six months before the intake
Applying to more than one institution simultaneously is allowed, but you must state it in the application form
alerts: No separate application to ADB exists - any portal or agent claiming to take an 'ADB application' is not ADB
There is no single deadline: the six-month rule is ADB's floor, but each designated institution's own intake date and deadline govern
The scholarship covers the scholar only - no spouse/dependent support, no family travel, no computers, no extra-curricular courses, no additional in-country travel
Scholars must return to and work in their home country for at least two years after completing studies, and a two-year employment restriction at the ADB Group applies
A second ADB-JSP award is not possible; between 1988 and 2025 the program awarded 4,600 scholarships, funded by US$228.4 million of Government of Japan financing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You submit the admission application plus the ADB-JSP Information Sheet and supporting documents to the designated institution at least six months before intake; the institution screens and ranks applicants, sends its ranked list with its grading system to ADB, ADB recommends awardees to Japan's Executive Director for formal approval, and the institution notifies all applicants and arranges the acceptance-of-award signing.
